newsitem.title: CANADA: Grain pools get financing for UGG bid.
newsitem.headline: Grain pools get financing for UGG bid.

text.p: The Alberta and Manitoba grain pools said on Monday they secured C$1.1 billion in financing from Bank of Nova Scotia, related to their C$172 million takeover bid for United Grain Growers Ltd.

"We've arranged C$1.1 billion through the Bank of Nova Scotia, financed over 18 months, for the pools' takeover bid of UGG and to retire UGG's debt," Alberta Wheat Pool chief financial officer Geoff Southwood told a news conference.
The pools' delegates on the weekend voted 98 percent in favor of the takeover, meeting Scotiabank's condition for the loan, Southwood said.
UGG has rejected the pools' offer.
Rival grain handlers have contacted the pools to inquire about purchasing UGG assets the pools would shed, Manitoba Pool general counsel Anders Bruun said.
Bruun would not identify the grain handlers, but said they included some companies that did not operate in the Canadian Prairies.
The Western Canadian Wheat Growers Association said on Monday it filed an objection with Canada's Competition Bureau over the takeover bid for UGG.
